items.title: Public Preview: JWT validation for Application Gateway for Containers
items.description:
Application Gateway for Containers now supports centralized JSON Web Token validation through the AuthPolicy custom resource. Teams can validate a token signature, issuer, lifetime, and configured audience by using signing keys retrieved from a trusted HTTPS JSON Web Key Set endpoint. Requests with missing or invalid credentials are rejected at the gateway instead of being forwarded to the backend. 

AuthPolicy can protect an ApplicationLoadBalancer, Gateway, HTTPRoute, GRPCRoute, or MCPRoute. Policies inherit through the resource hierarchy, while a more specific route-level policy can replace an inherited policy or explicitly opt a route out. Optional OAuth Protected Resource Metadata helps OAuth-aware clients discover authorization servers and supported scopes. 

  • Apply consistent JWT validation to HTTP, gRPC, and MCP routes 
  • Use Microsoft Entra ID or third-party identity providers that publish trusted JWKS signing keys 
  • Combine JWT validation with WAF so malicious traffic is inspected before authentication 
  • Publish OAuth resource metadata to enable authorization server discovery 

Learn more: 

  • JWT validation for Application Gateway for Containers 
  • Configure JWT validation for Application Gateway for Containers - Gateway API

items.title: Public Preview: MCP gateway for Application Gateway for Containers
items.description:
Application Gateway for Containers now supports Model Context Protocol routing through the new MCPRoute custom resource. Platform teams can publish MCP servers behind a stable hostname and path while centralizing TLS, JWT validation, Web Application Firewall protection, backend health monitoring, and routing policy at the gateway. 

MCPRoute supports both direct routing to a single MCP server and aggregation of multiple independent servers behind one logical endpoint. For aggregated deployments, Application Gateway for Containers merges tool, resource, and prompt discovery responses, namespaces capability names to avoid collisions, and routes invocations to the backend that owns the selected capability. 

  • Expose one governed endpoint for MCP clients and Kubernetes-hosted MCP servers 
  • Aggregate capabilities from multiple MCP servers  
  • Session affinity for MCP servers that maintain in-memory session state 
  • Apply JWT validation, WAF, backend TLS, health checks, and cross-namespace references 

Learn more: 

  • Model Context Protocol capabilities in Application Gateway for Containers 
  • Configure Model Context Protocol routing for Application Gateway for Containers

items.title: Public Preview: Private ingress for Application Gateway for Containers
items.description:
Application Gateway for Containers now supports private frontends that are reachable only through approved Azure Private Link private endpoints. This enables organizations to keep internal applications, shared services, and cross-cluster traffic on private connectivity while retaining Kubernetes-native Layer 7 routing, TLS, health probing, and Web Application Firewall capabilities. 

Private ingress supports connectivity across virtual networks, subscriptions, Microsoft Entra tenants, and Azure regions without requiring VNet peering. A single Application Gateway for Containers resource can also host public and private frontends, allowing teams to use separate exposure models and security policies for different workloads. 

  • Remove the public IP address and direct internet path from the frontend 
  • Enforce access through explicitly provisioned and approved private endpoints 
  •  Connect workloads across VNets, subscriptions, tenants, and regions, including environments with overlapping CIDR ranges  
  • Place an Azure Firewall, network virtual appliance, or another upstream service in front of Kubernetes workloads 

Learn more:   

  • Private ingress with Application Gateway for Containers  
  • Configure private ingress with Application Gateway for Containers - Gateway API

items.title: Public Preview: Advanced capacity insights are now available in Azure Storage Discovery
items.description:
Advanced capacity insights are now available for preview in Azure Storage Discovery. Storage Discovery now provides greater visibility into storage usage through insights such as access patterns, data age, storage tiers, object size distribution, retention states, and versioning. With these insights, teams can identify opportunities, understand factors contributing to storage growth, and inform storage management decisions at scale.

Learn more:

  • Discover what's new with advanced capacity insights
  • Explore advanced capacity insights and capabilities
  • Get started with Azure Storage Discovery

items.title: Public Preview: Extend immutability for PITR backups for Azure SQL Database and Azure SQL Managed Instance
items.description:
With this enhancement, you have the ability to lock your retention to the configured PITR retention, beyond the default 7 days of immutable backups that are already available. This is especially useful for financial customers who typically have 35 days of PITR retention. The current default immutability is up to 7 days, and with this enhancement you can extend and lock immutability up to 35 days.
Once locked, only extensions to PITR retention are allowed. This setting is permanent for the life of the database.

Learn more.

items.title: Generally Available: Enhanced Azure Site Recovery support for VMSS Flex
items.description:
Azure Site Recovery now offers an enhanced disaster recovery experience for virtual machines in Virtual Machine Scale Sets with flexible orchestration. The update improves target configuration and end-to-end recovery workflows, including failover, reprotection, and failback.

Learn more.
